notes: The pig fields are one bare field of rooted dust, about 110 by 64 m inside a low wall of piled field stones, with the three carob troughs in a straight row, the pen, the citizen's booth and fire and one lone carob; its east side ends in thorn scrub 67 to 72 m from the troughs, the owner's distant thorn scrub boundary.
The men at the estate wall wait in loose knots in the strip of morning shade, and the citizen walks the line beside them in the hard light.
Scene 1A's flash of the pigs at the trough and his own hand drifting toward the husks is the end of W09, over Asher's shoulder into the west trough.
The Scene 2 flash of the lamp coming up the black hill with the ewe across his father's shoulders cuts into W20 at 4.4 s; its source is Scene 2's W27 and W28.

He carries the pig the way his father carried the ewe, across his shoulders with its legs in his fists, and the camera walks ahead of him as Scene 2's W28 walks beside Eliab; the pig's flank is the W16 to W17 stitch, as the ewe's fleece is Scene 2's.

W15 rhymes Scene 2's signature move, the camera stopping at the trough while Asher goes after the lost one into the dark, as it stopped in the gateway while his father's lamp went down into the black valley.
W17 cuts to W18 on purpose, folding about 70 m of the carry across the black field into one break.

The soliloquy, W23 to W25, is the design note's chosen stillness on the exhausted face, at 2.2 words a second in the faint light of the citizen's low fire; its last 4 s ease back to him alone at the trough under the stars.

Asher sits facing home in the west-south-west and his father looks east down the road; the gate insert opens on the same stars that W21 ends on, and the dog lies at the gate as the design note keeps it there each dark.
